To determine the supremum of \(\int_{Z(v)} dS\), we consider the boundary behavior of harmonic functions in \(B\) that belong to \(C^\infty(\overline B)\). 

For any real-valued harmonic function \(v \in C^\infty(\overline B)\), the Cauchy data of \(v\) on the boundary \(\partial B\) consists of the Dirichlet data \(v|_{\partial B}\) and the Neumann data \(\partial_n v|_{\partial B}\). On the set 
\[
Z(v) = \{x \in \partial B : v(x) = \partial_{x_1} v(x) = \partial_{x_2} v(x) = \partial_{x_3} v(x) = 0\},
\]
both the function and all of its first-order partial derivatives vanish identically. In particular, both the Dirichlet data and the Neumann data vanish on \(Z(v)\).

By the boundary unique continuation properties for the Laplace operator (or by the uniqueness of the Cauchy problem for elliptic equations with analytic boundary), if a function \(v \in C^\infty(\overline B)\) harmonic in \(B\) has its Cauchy data vanishing on a set of positive surface measure on the sphere \(\partial B\), then \(v\) must be identically zero in \(B\). 

Since the problem restricts to nonzero functions \(v\), the set \(Z(v)\) must have surface measure zero for every such function:
\[
\int_{Z(v)} dS = 0.
\]
Taking the supremum over all such nonzero functions \(v\) yields \(0\).
